content: Recent studies have investigated the use of Geometric Algebra (GA) for modeling, analyzing, and controlling dynamical systems, with particular emphasis on electrical circuits. A key aspect of this methodology is transforming the ordinary differential equations that describe system behavior from the real domain into the Laplace domain. This transformation requires a rigorously defined Laplace transform within the framework of GA. In this work, we build upon prior research that extended the Laplace transform to certain hyper-complex algebras by presenting a definition of the Laplace transform specifically adapted to Geometric Algebra. Our formulation and its associated properties are applicable to geometric algebras with signatures up to and including 5.

Recent studies have explored the application of Geometric Algebra (GA) to the modeling, analysis, and control of dynamical systems, with a particular focus on electrical circuits. Central to this approach is the transformation of the ordinary differential equations governing system behavior from the real domain into the Laplace domain. Achieving this transformation necessitates a rigorously defined Laplace transform within the context of GA. In this work, we extend previous research that generalized the Laplace transform to certain hyper-complex algebras by providing a definition of the Laplace transform specifically tailored to Geometric Algebra. Our formulation, along with its associated properties, is valid for geometric algebras with signatures up to and including 5.
